title: A brief overview of methods for synthetic data for official statistics
summary: This report surveys methods for generating synthetic data for official statistics, aimed at Statistics Norway and other national statistics institutes, to enable safe and efficient data sharing while preserving both information value and privacy. It summarizes key references in the field, describing relational and deep-learning approaches to synthetic data generation. The Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) is described as a general synthetic data generator for relational databases, and CTGAN is mentioned among deep-learning-based synthetic data methods, both cited only as prior work rather than run.
evidence: Patki et al. (2016) proposed a general synthetic data generator, which they named the Synthetic Data Vault, to synthesise complete tables of a relational database.
needs: Full text not obtained; only abstract and citing sentences available, so depth of engagement with SDV/CTGAN beyond brief description cannot be confirmed.

title: CTGAN VS TGAN? Which one is more suitable for generating synthetic EEG data
summary: This work empirically compares two GAN-based tabular synthesizers, TGAN and CTGAN, to determine which better generates synthetic EEG signal data, showing sample outputs from each model. The comparison is framed as a direct evaluation of generator quality for a biomedical time-series/tabular use case. CTGAN, the SDV-family conditional tabular GAN, is run as one of the two generators being compared against TGAN.

title: Domain-Aware Tabular Data Augmentation Using Large Language Models
summary: This work proposes an LLM-based domain-aware tabular data augmentation method that encodes scientific constraints via policy generation, applied to an imbalanced geochemical rock classification dataset where closure constraints and correlations must be preserved. It outperforms SMOTE, Gaussian sampling, and no-augmentation baselines in accuracy and macro-F1. CTGAN is named only in a background sentence listing deep generative models (alongside TVAE and CTAB-GAN) used for tabular synthetic data generation, without being run or evaluated.
evidence: "Deep generative models for tabular data such as Variational Autoencoders (TVAE) (7) and Generative Adversarial Networks (CTGAN, CTAB-GAN) (8; 9) learn complex data distributions for synthetic data generation."
needs: Full text not available; unclear whether CTGAN is used experimentally beyond this background sentence, though abstract's baselines (SMOTE, Gaussian sampling) do not mention it.

title: Generating Privacy-Preserving Synthetic Tabular Data Using Oblivious Variational Autoencoders
summary: This paper proposes an oblivious variational autoencoder architecture for generating privacy-preserving synthetic tabular data, aiming to protect sensitive attributes while retaining statistical utility. It benchmarks its model against state-of-the-art deep generative baselines including medGAN, VEEGAN, tableGAN, CTGAN, and TVAE, and adopts mode-specific normalization (MSN) from CTGAN's methodology to preprocess multi-modal continuous variables. SDV's CTGAN and TVAE are run as comparison baselines, with TVAE singled out as the strongest competitor, while CTGAN's mode-specific normalization technique is also incorporated into the authors' own preprocessing pipeline.
evidence: "In an extensive empirical comparison, TVAE outperforms CTGAN and other state-of-the-art GAN models, and is a frontrunner that we compare against." The paper also preprocesses continuous variables using "mode-specific normalization (MSN) (Xu et al., 2019)" adopted from CTGAN's design.
needs: Full text not obtained; unclear whether CTGAN/TVAE were run via the sdv-dev library itself or via the authors' own implementation of the published methodology.

title: Mitigating Bias in Medical Datasets: A Comparative Analysis of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) Based Data Generation Techniques
summary: This paper compares several GAN variants -- including MedGAN, MC-MedGAN, TGAN and CTGAN -- for generating balanced synthetic data to reduce bias in medical datasets, evaluating three medical datasets and finding MedGAN performs best. CTGAN and TGAN are introduced in the background section as tabular-data GAN variants and appear among the models the study's abstract says were evaluated for producing balanced data. CTGAN (and its precursor TGAN) are treated as one of several generative baselines compared against the authors' preferred MedGAN approach.

title: MTCopula: Synthetic Complex Data Generation Using Copula
summary: This conference paper proposes MTCopula, a new copula-based method for generating synthetic complex/mixed-type data, motivated by the observation that most prior copula-based synthetic data approaches rely solely on the Gaussian copula paired with Pearson correlation. It positions itself as departing from this limitation by modeling dependencies and marginal behaviors more flexibly. The original SDV paper is cited as one of the prior contributions exemplifying this Gaussian-copula-only approach that the authors' method improves upon.

title: Privacy-sensitive Business Models: Barriers of Organizational Adoption of Privacy-Enhancing Technologies
summary: This paper reviews the literature on organizational barriers to adopting privacy-enhancing technologies (PETs) in data-driven business models, using the TOE (Technology-Organization-Environment) framework to explain why firms resist PET adoption despite calls from research streams to use them. title: Synthetic Data for Machine Learning in Pharmacology: Utility, Privacy, and Clinical Validity in Precision Therapeutics: A narrative review
summary: A narrative methodological review surveying synthetic-data generation approaches for pharmacology and therapeutic drug monitoring, covering sequential statistical models, Bayesian networks, copula-based methods, deep tabular generators, patient-centric local methods, and mechanistic pharmacometric simulations, alongside evaluation criteria (statistical fidelity, task-based utility, privacy risk, pharmacological plausibility). title: Synthetic Tabular Data Generation with Oblivious Variational Autoencoders : Alleviating the Paucity of Personal Tabular Data for Open Research
summary: This paper proposes an Oblivious Variational Autoencoder (OVAE) for generating synthetic tabular data, aimed at easing the scarcity of personal (e.g., health) tabular datasets available for open research while protecting privacy. It benchmarks OVAE against deep generative baselines including medGAN, VEEGAN, tableGAN, CTGAN and TVAE, and adopts CTGAN's mode-specific normalization technique to preprocess multi-modal continuous variables. CTGAN and TVAE, from the SDV family, are run as comparison baselines and their mode-specific normalization concept is incorporated into the authors' own preprocessing pipeline.

title: STAN: Synthetic Network Traffic Generation using Autoregressive Neural Models
summary: STAN proposes an autoregressive neural architecture combining CNN and mixture density network layers to synthesize network traffic data, capturing both temporal dependence and inter-attribute dependence for continuous and discrete variables, evaluated against simulated and real traffic datasets and downstream anomaly-detection tasks. In its related-work discussion the authors describe CTGAN as a GAN-based approach for generating general tabular data with mixed discrete/continuous attributes, contrasting it with Bayesian-network approaches, and cite vine copulas among traditional modeling algorithms limited by distributional assumptions. Both SDV-family methods (CTGAN and vine copulas) are discussed and critiqued as prior art rather than run in the experiments described.

title: Synthetic Data -- A Privacy Mirage
summary: This paper introduces an evaluation framework for quantifying the privacy gain of publishing synthetic data versus raw data, measuring re-identification and attribute disclosure risks across generative models ranging from simple histograms to differentially private GANs. It finds synthetic data offers little privacy protection even under weak adversarial assumptions, challenging claims that synthetic data is inherently privacy-preserving. CTGAN is discussed as an example generative model, with its mode-specific normalisation of tabular attributes described as a technique for approximating complex distributions through GANs.
evidence: "With CTGAN, Xu et al. [35] introduce mode-specific normalisation of tabular data attributes to improve the approximation of complex distributions through GANs."

title: Anomaly Detection in Railway Radio Signaling: Synthetic Data Generation and AI-Based Models
summary: This thesis develops an automated Radio Network Anomaly Detection tool for Wi-Fi planning on the Torino Linea 1 metro line, combining Autoencoder, Gaussian Mixture Model, and Isolation Forest techniques to flag anomalous radio signal behavior. To address the scarcity of anomaly-free data in early design phases, it builds a synthetic data generation pipeline, testing multiple models and finding that a Tabular Variational Autoencoder (TVAE) paired with a rejection sampling strategy guided by a Random Forest discriminator is most effective. SDV's TVAE is run as the core synthetic data generator underpinning the whole anomaly-detection pipeline.
evidence: "The combination of a Tabular Variational Autoencoder (TVAE) with a rejection sampling strategy, guided by a Random Forest discriminator, emerged as the most effective pipeline, significantly enhancing the performance of anomaly detection models."

title: Towards automatically linking data elements
